== Biography ==
James was born about 1828. <ref>Age 73 in 1901 census.</ref>
He was the son of James Glasgow and lived at Ballynasollus, Kildress as of 1873.
<ref name="m"/>

On 10 May 1873  at 3rd Cookstown Presbyterian, he married Rachel Bell of Ballynasollus, Kildress, daughter of Richard Bell, farmer.
<ref name="m">[https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/details-civil/df5ba32798387 James Glasgow, Rachel Bell, 10 May 1873, Cookstown] at Irish Civil Registration - Marriages</ref>

He passed away 7 Sep 1907 age 78 and was interred at Clare Churchyard.
<ref>PRONI Will Calendars: "Administration of the Estate of James Glasgow late of Ballinasallos County Tyrone Farmer who died 7 September 1907 granted at Armagh to William John Glasgow Farmer."</ref>
<ref>[https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/viewer/bl/0002006/19070914/030/0002 "Funeral of Mr James Glasgow, Ballynasollus"]. ''Mid-Ulster Mail'' - Saturday 14 September 1907, Page 2</ref>
The chief mourners were:
* [[Glasgow-1683|William John Glasgow]] (son)
* [[Glasgow-1688|Maggie]] and [[Glasgow-1686|Sarah Glasgow]] (daughters)
* [[Glasgow-1795|Thomas Glasgow]] (brother)
* David Glasgow, [[Boone-5401|Andrew Boon]] (brothers-in-law)
* David Glasgow (cousin)
* Jane Glasgow (niece)
* W J Glasgow, RIchard Glasgow, W J Dorrage , Samuel Glasgow, Samuel H Glasgow, Henry Bell, Richard Bell (nephews)
A marriage for James Glasgow and Bell was registered on 10 May 1873 in the Cookstown district.<ref>[https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/marriage GRONI civil marriage index], 10 May 1873, Cookstown district, M/1873/L1/1131/2/71.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1702]] is assessed at 96% (proved). James’s 1873 marriage names James Glasgow as father and places him at Ballynasollus. His funeral calls Thomas his brother, and Thomas’s role at the elder James’s death provides a strong identity bridge to the selected father.

Held citation and associated narrative supports this specific paternal assessment; no original was newly inspected.

Next useful test: Correlate the 1873 father occupation with elder James’s 1882 death informant.

Source basis already held: [https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/details-civil/df5ba32798387 On 10 May 1873 at 3rd Cookstown Presbyterian, he married Rachel Bell of Ballynasollus, Kildress, daughter of Richard Bell, farmer.  James Glasgow, Rachel Bell, 10 May 1873, Cookstown (https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/details-civil/df5ba32798387) at Irish Civil Registration - Marriages]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.


There was another couple James Glasgow / Rachel Bell of the similar part of Tyrone. We have selected the linked 1901 census below because the other [[Bell-32242|Rachel Bell]] has a known age (age 18 in 1857) which matches a lot closer to the other census of James Glasgow / Rachel.

I've added to this couple all the children born at Ballynasollus (which does line up nicely with the census below).  Other children to James Glasgow/Rachel Bell at other places have gone to the other couple.
